gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple's 18-hour rating for the Apple Watch SE 3 GPS + Cellular counts only 4 hours on cellular and 14 hours connected to an iPhone, or that Apple's only all-day figure with cellular on the whole time is 16 hours (the Apple Watch For Your Kids test). Samsung's footnote gives no runtime split between phone and LTE, and Notebookcheck found the Galaxy Watch8 LTE 'won't last a whole day' with no phone nearby.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rivals. support.apple.com/en-us/119601 says only that 'Turning on cellular for extended periods uses more battery power' and gives no hours. Samsung CA's setup page does not mention battery life. The Apple Watch For Your Kids, family-member setup, Verizon and T-Mobile results in the list cover setup, not battery. None of them breaks a maker's rating into time on cellular versus time tethered to a phone. Samsung CA already says Wear OS Galaxy watches need a phone for first setup, so the setup point is only partly new. The new part is the battery normalisation.
decides: This confirms the Apple Watch SE 3 as the pick for someone who wants to leave the phone behind all day. It is the only candidate whose maker publishes a test with cellular on all day: up to 16 hours with a 5-minute call, a 30-minute workout and Find My sharing. Samsung publishes no such figure, and Notebookcheck says the Watch8 LTE won't last a full day away from the phone. Two cells on our page need fixing. (1) The battery column should show runtime away from the phone, with the maker's tethered rating in a footnote. (2) The Galaxy Watch 8 'setup' cell is wrong. Samsung's own footnote says activation works only after connecting to a smartphone with Google Mobile Services, and Samsung CA says Wear OS models can't be set up without a phone. Its 'Android 6.0+' entry is also wrong: Samsung says Android 12 or later with more than 1.5 GB of memory.

findings.label: Test behind the 18-hour all-day rating
findings.value: 18 h = 4 h on cellular + 14 h connected to iPhone via Bluetooth
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'a total of 4 hours of cellular connection and 14 hours of connection to iPhone via Bluetooth' over 18 h. The test also includes 300 time checks, 90 notifications, 15 min of app use and a 60-min workout with music. 4 of 18 h means 22% of the rated day is away from the phone.

findings.label: Test behind the 32-hour Low Power Mode rating
findings.value: 32 h = on-demand cellular + 24 h connected to iPhone via Bluetooth (includes 6 h of sleep tracking)
findings.note: 430 time checks, 130 notifications, 20 min of app use and a 60-min workout with music. Cellular is 'on-demand', so this figure does not describe a day without the phone.

findings.label: Battery with cellular on all day (Apple Watch For Your Kids test)
findings.note: Test: '80 time checks, 50 notifications, 22 minutes of app use, a 5-minute phone call, and a 30-minute workout with music playback ... over the course of 16 hours with cellular connection and Find My location sharing enabled', on a preproduction SE 3 GPS + Cellular. This is the closest maker figure to a day without a phone. It is 2 h less than the headline 18 h, and the usage is lighter.

findings.label: Workout tracking without iPhone
findings.note: 'Workout tested without iPhone and with heart rate sensor on during outdoor run workout sessions.' Apple does not say whether cellular was on.

findings.label: Music playback from watch storage
findings.note: Music played from the watch's storage over Bluetooth, not streamed over cellular.

findings.label: Phone requirement
findings.value: iPhone 11 or later with iOS 27 or later; wireless service plan required for cellular
findings.note: From the buy page's footnote 2 and FAQ. Our page says 'iPhone 11 or later'; add iOS 27.

findings.label: Carrier rule for the watch line
findings.value: The iPhone and watch must use the same carrier, except watches set up through Apple Watch For Your Kids
findings.source_title: Set up cellular on Apple Watch - Apple Support
findings.note: This is the cited rival page (published 2026-09-14). It gives no battery hours; it says only 'Turning on cellular for extended periods uses more battery power.'

findings.label: Battery test footnote
findings.value: 40mm battery is 325 mAh (typical). Samsung says battery life comes from 'internal lab tests for typical usage pattern scenarios' and gives no hours or LTE/Bluetooth split
findings.source_title: Samsung Galaxy Watch8 Series: Ultra Comfort, from Sleep to Workout - Samsung Mobile Press
findings.note: Footnote 14. Footnote 15 says the charging test used pre-release BT and LTE watches 'each paired to a Samsung phone'. Unlike Apple, Samsung does not say how much of the rated time was spent off the phone.

findings.label: Can it be activated without a phone
findings.value: No. 'Device activation is only available after connecting to a smartphone that supports Google Mobile Services'
findings.source_title: Samsung Galaxy Watch8 Series: Ultra Comfort, from Sleep to Workout - Samsung Mobile Press
findings.note: Footnote 19. This contradicts our current 'setup' cell ('Samsung allows standalone setup on LTE models'). Samsung CA (cited rival, read the same day) agrees: only Galaxy Watch, Watch Active, Active2 and Watch3 can be set up without a phone, and Wear OS models (Watch4 and later) need a compatible phone for initial setup.

findings.label: Phone compatibility
findings.value: Android 12 or later with more than 1.5 GB of memory
findings.source_title: Samsung Galaxy Watch8 Series: Ultra Comfort, from Sleep to Workout - Samsung Mobile Press
findings.note: Footnote 16. Our page says 'Android 6.0+', which is wrong. Sleep features on samsung.com/us require Android 11 or later with 1.5 GB; the press release's Android 12 requirement is the stricter one.

findings.label: Measured runtime, phone nearby versus away
findings.value: 24 h with AOD and phone connected most of the time; about 1.5 days without AOD; 'won't last for a whole day' when used a long time without the phone nearby
findings.source_title: Brighter and slimmer: Samsung Galaxy Watch8 LTE smartwatch review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck tested the 44 mm model (435 mAh) with all health features, workout detection and an eSIM. It gives no hour figure for use away from the phone. The 40 mm has 325 mAh, about 25% less capacity, so expect less.
